chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام delivered a sermon on the day of Eid al-Fitr and said:
"All praise belongs to Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve set up equals with their Lord."
We do not associate anything with Allah, and we do not take any guardian besides Him.

"All praise belongs to Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs all praise in the world and the Hereafter; and He is the All-wise, the All-aware. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it, and He is the All-merciful, the All-forgiving."
"There is no god but He; to Him is the return."
And praise belongs to Allah, the One who
"holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed Allah is surely most kind and merciful to mankind."

O Allah, have mercy on us by Your mercy and encompass us with Your forgiveness; surely You are the Most High, the Most Great. And praise belongs to Allah, from whose mercy none is despaired, from whose blessing none is excluded, from whose relief none is made hopeless, and from whose worship none may turn away; by His word the seven heavens stood, the outspread earth became settled, the firm mountains were fixed, the fertilizing winds blew, the clouds moved in the atmosphere of the sky, and the seas stood within their bounds. He is the God over them and the Subduer; the mighty are humbled before Him, the arrogant become small before Him, and the worlds submit to Him willingly and unwillingly. We praise Him as He praised Himself and as He deserves; we seek His help, His forgiveness, and His guidance, and we bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone without partner. He knows what souls conceal, what the seas cover, what darkness hides, and no hidden thing is absent from Him.
from a tree, nor any grain in darknesses, except that He knows it. There is no god but He.
"And neither anything fresh nor dry except that it is in a clear book."

And He knows what the doers do, along what course they proceed, and to what turning-place they will return. We seek guidance from Allah through guidance, and we bear witness that Muhammad is His servant, His Prophet, and His Messenger to His creation, His trustee over His revelation; that he conveyed the messages of his Lord, strove for Allah against those who deviated from Him and those who set equals with Him, and worshipped Allah until certainty came to him. May Allah bless him and his family.

I counsel you, O servants of Allah, to have taqwa of Allah, from whom no blessing departs, from whom no mercy is exhausted, whom the servants can never do without, and whose blessings deeds can never repay. He encouraged taqwa, made the world seem little, warned against acts of disobedience, is exalted through everlastingness, and humbled His creation through death and passing away. Death is the end of creatures and the path of all beings, tied to the forelocks of those who remain; the fleeing of runaways cannot frustrate it, and when it comes it captures the people of desire, demolishes every pleasure, removes every blessing, and cuts off every delight. The world is an abode for which Allah has decreed passing away and for whose people He has decreed departure from it; yet most people intend its permanence and magnify its structure. It is sweet and green, hastening to the seeker and clinging to the heart of the beholder; the wealthy miser withholds from the weak, and the fearful anxious person finds it bitter. So depart from it, may Allah have mercy on you, in the best way available to you; do not seek from it more than a little, do not ask of it beyond sufficiency, be content with a small share, do not stretch your eyes toward what the luxurious have been given, make light of it, do not settle in it, and weary yourselves in it. Beware of luxury, diversion, and delicacies, for in that are heedlessness and delusion. Indeed, the world has become estranged, turned away, become sweetened, and announced a farewell. Indeed, the Hereafter has journeyed and come forward, loomed near, and announced its appearance. Indeed, the training-ground is today and the race is tomorrow. Indeed, the prize is the Garden and the end is the Fire. Is there then no repenter from his sin before the day of his death? Is there no worker for himself before the day of his misery and poverty? May Allah make us and you among those who fear Him and hope for His reward.

Indeed, this day is a day Allah has made an Eid for you and made you worthy of it. So remember Allah and He will remember you, and call upon Him and He will answer you. And pay your fitrah, for it is the sunnah of your Prophet and an obligatory duty from your Lord. Let every person among you discharge it for himself and for all his dependents, male and female, young and old, free and enslaved: on behalf of each person among them, one sa' of wheat, or one sa' of dates, or one sa' of barley. And obey Allah regarding what Allah has made obligatory upon you and commanded you of establishing salat, giving zakat, hajj of the House, fasting the month of Ramadan, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and doing good to your women and those whom your right hands possess. And obey Allah regarding what He has forbidden you from: slandering the chaste woman, committing indecency, drinking wine, giving short measure, reducing the scale, false testimony, and fleeing from the battlefield. May Allah protect us and you through taqwa, and make the Hereafter better for us and for you than the first life.
Indeed, the best discourse and the most eloquent admonition for the Godwary is the mighty, wise Book of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan:
"In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. Say: He, Allah, is One. Allah is the Self-Sufficient. He neither begot nor was begotten. And there is none comparable to Him."
Then he sits briefly, like the sitting of one in haste, then rises for the sermon.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, portrayed here as transient, deceptive, and passing away.
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: Zakat, the obligatory alms due as part of Allah’s commands.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Salat, the prescribed ritual prayer established as a divine obligation.
key_terms.الْآخِرَةَ: The Hereafter, the lasting abode toward which all people are moving.
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ: That which is right and recognized as good, to be enjoined.
key_terms.الْمُنْكَرِ: That which is wrong and objectionable, to be forbidden.
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness and pious guarding of oneself through obedience to Allah.
key_terms.فِطْرَتَكُمْ: Your Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms given at Eid al-Fitr.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali عليه السلام teach in his Eid al-Fitr sermon about tawhid, the Hereafter, and Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: This sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام on Eid al-Fitr joins tawhid, praise of Allah, remembrance of death, detachment from the world, and practical commands related to Zakat al-Fitr and core religious duties. It emphasizes Allah’s absolute knowledge and power, the urgency of repentance and preparation for the Hereafter, and the sanctity of divine obligations and prohibitions.
